intent: Bottom navigation bar for phone-width layouts (Material NavigationBar equivalent): a 56px frosted-glass bar of 3–5 evenly-spread top-level destinations, each an icon over an 11px label with a pill indicator behind the active item's icon. Use exactly one per page, only for top-level destinations — fewer than 3 wants tabs, more than 5 wants a sidebar or rail. The base bar is static; add .bottom-nav-fixed to pin it to the bottom of the viewport.

structure.description: One <a> per destination (3–5 of them), flexed to equal widths. Mark the current destination with .active — exactly one.
20px icon slot (inline SVG sized to fill). The selection pill (32×20, selected-bg) and the hover wash render behind it via ::before.
11px label under the icon; truncates. Omit only when the icon is universally understood — then give the item an aria-label.

aria.when: The page contains more than one <nav> landmark — label each to distinguish them.

allowedIn: directly under <body>, after the page content

a11yNotes: Use a real <nav> element with <a> children so the bar is a landmark of links. Put aria-current="page" on the active item. Icons are decorative — aria-hidden="true" on the SVG — because the label carries the name; if you drop the label, move the name to aria-label on the item. Like the navbar this is a glass surface: never nest another glass surface inside it, and when using .bottom-nav-fixed give the scrolling content enough bottom padding that nothing hides behind the bar.
examples: HomeSearchProfile
